blocks.prompt: 9. The Governor of the Punjab calls a meeting of 14 officers. In how many ways can they be seated at a round table?
blocks.explanation:
14 officers at a round table: a plain circular permutation.
Plan: fix one officer and arrange the other 13 (Case-I).
steps:
Given: 14 officers, round table.
To find: the number of seatings.
Method: \(n\) different people round a table can be seated in \((n - 1)!\) ways (clockwise and anticlockwise orders are different at a meeting).

Apply the formula
\[(14 - 1)! = 13!\]
Why: Rotating all officers one seat gives the same seating, so one officer is fixed.

Check
\[14! \div 14 = \dfrac{87178291200}{14}\]
\[= 6227020800 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Each circular seating appears as 14 rotations among the 14! row seatings. The book's answer counts only the 14 officers; if the Governor also sat at the table there would be 15 people and 14! ways.
